newsitem.title: USA: EL Paso unit says Pakistan project begins.
newsitem.headline: EL Paso unit says Pakistan project begins.

text.p: El Paso Energy International Co, a unit of El Paso Energy Corp, said Thursday construction has began on a 151-megawatt combined cycle power plant in Kabirwala, Punjab Province, in Pakistan.

The El Paso unit said it will hold a 42 percent stake in the power plant while Fauji Foundation of Pakistan and the Asian Development Bank will hold stakes of 45 percent and 13 percent, respectively, it said.
Financing for the $170-million was arranged and syndicated by the Manila-based Asian Development Bank and the Dutch bank ABN Amro, it said.
Construction, engineering and procurement for the project is being undertaken by Pakistan's National Energy Production Corp on a 22-month construction schedule, it said.

Pakistan's state-owned Oil & Gas Development Corp will supply natural gas to fuel the plant and the nation's Water and Power Development Authority will buy power from the plant under a 30-year contract, it said.
Power sales are expected to begin November 1, 1998, it said.

Byron Kelley, executive vice president of the El Paso unit, said that with the project, the company now has onwership interests in over 1,600 MW of power-generating capacity currently operating or under construction in the U.S., Mexico, Peru, Indonesia, Hungary and Pakistan."
